text:
maya: Quick update — ran a focused sweep this morning comparing SSE (server-sent events) vs non-streaming poll/batched HTTP across A100 (us-west2) and H100 (eu-west1). Posting raw notes and a tiny ASCII summary. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

maya: TL;DR: SSE gives much better median latency for interactive traffic (single-request low-token workloads). Polling + batching gives higher sustained token throughput at the cost of higher p95/p99 latency. Region/kernel and quantization change the break-even point a lot.

tj: Nice. Which kernels did you test? and what quant levels?

maya: Kernels: matmul-opt (default), fused-attn-v2 (H100-optimized), and nvfuser path on A100 where applicable. Quant: fp16 baseline, q4f16, q8_0 (experimental). Also tried small KV-cache tweak (prefetch=1).

santiago: Any surprising region diffs?

maya: Yes — H100 eu-west1 with fused-attn-v2 + q4f16 gave ~1.8–2x token/sec vs A100 fp16 for long seqs (seq=2048). But H100 p95 on SSE slightly worse if the kernel falls back (we saw jank on warmup). A100 was actually more consistent on tail with matmul-opt + prefetch=1.

maya: Short numbers (single-shot gen, seq=512, prompt=64, concurrency 32)

maya: ASCII table:

| mode | GPU | p50 | p95 | sustained tokens/s (approx) | notes |
| SSE  | A100 | 34ms | 180ms | 16k tok/s | lower median, stable tail |
| POLL | A100 | 70ms | 220ms | 36k tok/s | batching increases throughput |
| SSE  | H100 | 28ms | 240ms | 28k tok/s | better throughput but tail spikes |
| POLL | H100 | 66ms | 300ms | 52k tok/s | best tokens/s with q4f16 + fused-attn-v2 |

tj: So polling wins tokens/sec but loses on p95 — expected. Where's the break-even rps for choosing SSE vs poll?

maya: For our workload (avg prompt ~120 tokens), break-even is around 200–300 concurrent users per shard on A100; on H100 it's ~400–600 concurrent due to better kernel throughput but more volatile tails. In practice: if you require p95 < 250ms for interactive, go SSE/cold-start-friendly configs and smaller batch windows. If you optimize for cost and bulk inference (embs or batch scoring), use poll with batching + q4f16.

santiago: Any quality regressions from q4f16?

maya: Minimal on our eval set: ROUGE-like auto metrics showed ~2–3% drop on long-form summarization. For short chat turns it's <1% and often indistinguishable. We flagged a small failure mode on numeric accuracy — put a regression alert for that eval.

evaluator-bot: alert: eval/regressions/longform-summaries flagged q4f16 drop = 3.1% (threshold 2.0%). See /evals/1830001112-longform-q4f16.json

tj: Can you paste the benchmark command so I can reproduce?

maya: Repro snippet:

```
./bench --model /models/redwood-generic-v1 --quant q4f16 --mode sse --region eu-west1 --gpus h100 --concurrency 32 --seq 512 --report perf.json
./bench --model /models/redwood-generic-v1 --quant q4f16 --mode poll --batch 16 --region eu-west1 --gpus h100 --concurrency 128 --seq 512 --report perf-poll.json
```

maya: Logs (trimmed):

```
[2026-03-19T08:12:03Z] worker0 H100 fused-attn-v2 warmup done, p50=30ms, p95=220ms
[2026-03-19T08:12:19Z] worker0 SSE steady-state tokens/s=27500
[2026-03-19T08:13:05Z] worker1 POLL batch=16 tokens/s=52000 p95=300ms
```

tj: Nice. Any config knobs to reduce H100 tail on SSE?

maya: A few that helped in tests:
- enable thread-pinning for the inference pipeline
- set kv_prefetch=1 (reduces page-in stalls)
- warm kernels by running dynamic padding step 1s before accepting traffic
- on H100, prefer fused-attn-v2 but add a fallback timeout of 120ms to matmul-opt on slow warmups

santiago: Could we surface a routing rule in the console: region+gpu -> prefer poll for batch-heavy routes, SSE for interactive routes?

maya: Yes, that's exactly what I prototyped. Rule-ish: 
- route.interactive -> SSE, max_batch_window_ms=25, concurrency_limit=64
- route.batch -> POLL, batch_size=16-32, quant_recommendation=q4f16 for H100
